# 03 A sequence diagram stops swallowing activation markers

## Outcome

`A->>+B: x` and `B-->>-A: y` are rejected with a diagnostic saying activation is not drawn yet,
instead of parsing cleanly into a message with no activation recorded.

## Why this ticket exists

`MESSAGE_RE` carries `[+-]?` between the arrow and the target, and the parser has a comment saying
so deliberately: activation bars are a spec non-goal, and rather than reject the whole document,
the marker is matched and discarded.

**That comment is the clearest statement of the old policy in the codebase, and this board
overturns it.** The reasoning was sound when Siren supported a subset: a swallowed `+` cost the
author one feature and kept the rest of their diagram. Under the absolute condition it costs them
the signal that anything is missing, and it makes the diagram *wrong* — Mermaid draws an
activation bar and a lifeline that visibly thickens; Siren draws neither and says nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `A->>+B: x` produces an error-severity diagnostic naming activation. So does `A->>-B: x`.
- [x] The message says activation is **not drawn yet**, not that the line is unrecognized. The
      author wrote valid Mermaid; the honest answer names the gap rather than blaming the input.
- [x] Every arrow token still parses without a marker. All ten forms — assert the set, because the
      change is inside the shared `MESSAGE_RE` and `-x` / `--x` end in a character the marker
      class does not contain but a careless fix might.
- [x] `examples/sequence-*.srn` still render with zero diagnostics. They use `-x` and `--x`
      legitimately; confirm rather than assume.
- [x] **`parseSiren.test.ts:286` asserts the behavior this ticket reverses** — it feeds `A->>+B`
      and expects zero diagnostics, with an inline note calling the shorthand "NOT parsed
      specially". Update it and call it out in your report as the intended change; it is the only
      test that pins the old policy.
- [x] The parser comment explaining the swallow is **replaced**, not amended. It argues for a
      policy this board reverses, and a comment arguing the opposite of what the code does is
      worse than none.
- [x] The corpus's `seq-activation-shorthand` entry moves from `silently-wrong` to `rejected`.
      The literals as you inherit them are `SILENTLY_WRONG = 3` and `REJECTED = 38`; after this
      ticket they are **2 and 39**. The 2 left are `seq-loop` and `seq-alt-else`, whose exit is
      implementation rather than rejection — **do not touch them**, and note that after this
      ticket `silently-wrong` has reached the floor this board can reach.
- [x] `activate` / `deactivate` as standalone statements stay rejected as they are today — they
      are a separate gap on a later board, and this ticket must not half-implement them.

## Status

Done (2026-09-06), commit e5cbb13. 3 slices, all red-green. 687 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean
both. Ratchets: silently-wrong 3 → **2**, rejected 38 → **39**.

`silently-wrong` has reached this board's floor. The 2 left are `seq-loop` and `seq-alt-else`,
named in the ratchet's own comment, whose exit is drawing a block's keyword rather than refusing
the construct.

Integrator verified independently: both markers refused by name, `activate` unchanged, and all ten
arrow tokens still parse markerless with zero diagnostics.
